28	## Scope
29	
30	The word "durable" covers three different designs in the agent stack, and they fail in different
31	ways. This entry keeps them apart, then records the measured failure of the guarantee that
32	frameworks document but do not deliver. It draws on one vendor's runtime contract, one Chinese
33	cloud vendor's managed-agent runtime, two research papers, and one Japanese-language engineering
34	statement of the constraint model.
35	
36	## A. Durable execution as a runtime discipline
37	
38	A run is a sequence of *durable operations*; the runtime checkpoints the outcome of each and
39	replays the sequence on restart, substituting checkpointed results for completed operations
40	instead of re-executing them.
41	
42	The Japanese-language statement of the boundary rule: side-effecting and non-deterministic work
43	must be confined inside a durable operation so that replay cannot corrupt it; and replay must
44	traverse the *same* operation sequence — the Japanese implementation verifies each step's
45	identity against the existing checkpoint and treats a mismatch as non-deterministic execution
46	and errors out rather than continuing. This is a community row and therefore tier B; it is used
47	for the engineering framing, not as authority for the mechanism.
48	
49	## B. Durable execution as a runtime substrate
50	
51	Temporal's own contract shows what the discipline demands of the substrate. The server *cannot*
52	detect a worker crash, so the **Start-To-Close Timeout is the thing that forces a retry** — not
53	health checking. And an unset Heartbeat Timeout and an explicit `0s` are indistinguishable once
54	the Activity is scheduled, so "no heartbeat" cannot be expressed as a distinct policy. The
55	heartbeat throttle interval is derived rather than chosen: `min(heartbeatTimeout × 0.8,
56	maxHeartbeatThrottleInterval)`, default 30 s with a 60 s ceiling.
57	
58	**Overlap with a held row, stated.** The lane already holds this page as S117 under the
59	worker-liveness scope. The capture is byte-identical to S117's (same sha256), so the two rows
60	are one document under two scopes; the group is pinned in `.ufo/pins/source-dupes.json` rather
61	than left as an unpinned census warning. This entry adds only the *retry-forcing* half of the
62	page — the Start-To-Close Timeout — to what the lane already held about the heartbeat half.
63	
64	## C. Durable execution as a managed, server-side session
65	
66	A Chinese cloud vendor's managed-agent runtime takes the third shape: the platform holds the
67	session state and persists the event history server-side; each session runs in its own managed
68	cloud container sandbox; and the event model is a **session-level SSE stream**, not
69	response-level streaming. An interrupted long-running task can therefore be resumed. This is a
70	vendor's own product contract — it asserts the behaviour rather than measuring it.
71	
72	## D. Where the guarantees break
73	
74	Across six widely used open-source agent frameworks, the documented barrier contract — while a
75	run is paused, cancelled or timed out, no gated side effect executes — holds on none of them. The
76	recurring failure is a **sibling leak**: an approval gate suspends its own branch while a
77	sibling's effect executes during the pause, which defeats rejection outright. The same probes
78	confirm replay double-execution, cancellation orphans and timeout zombies.
79	
80	The hazard is reachable in practice rather than theoretical: frontier models emit the
81	leak-triggering plan shape at rates up to 14%, and live models driving unmodified frameworks
82	leaked **215 of 1,200 runs**. The proposed repair is an *environment-external* gate through which
83	every side effect must be admitted, enforcing hold-until-decided, reject-cancels,
84	dedup-on-replay and fence-on-cancel under a stated complete-mediation contract.
85	
86	## E. Where exactly-once has to live
87	
88	The companion question — when an agent's tool call is duplicated, which layer owns the fix — is
89	posed by the paper whose title attributes duplicate side effects jointly to the model, the
90	harness *and* the tool contract, and which names its benchmark "Limbo".
91	
92	**Scope limit, stated rather than hidden:** this round read the **title page only** of that
93	paper (arXiv abs page, HTTP 200, 44,818 bytes). No measured result from it is claimed here. The
94	campaign's own `S141` row for the same document claims the 25,930-episode measurement; the lane
95	does not adopt that row, because the campaign staged the same document under two ids and
96	adopting both would count one paper twice — the reject and its flip are recorded in
97	`corpus/lessons/round-60.md`.
98	
99	## Consequence for an orchestrator
100
